attribution.evidence: plain main (b223a862, no agriculture-b) reproduces churn signature within a partial ~14-day warring_states seed=1337 run: SurvivalMergeIn Team70→Team37 repeated 3x + Team70→Team11 1x, before the run was killed by GODOT_TIMEOUT
attribution.interpretation: agriculture-b's popcap mechanism amplifies volume/speed (more desperate teams sooner) but does not create the bug; mechanism lives in main's JOIN resolver, confirmed by code-read (JOIN timeout/abort_ghost added by this fix touch faction_ai_system.gd only, not agriculture-b files)
attribution.consequence: direct branch-vs-base-main comparison is valid; churn-rich (agriculture-b overlay) condition not required for attribution

1_release_no_repeat.verdict: PROVEN via deterministic control bed (mergein_join_lifecycle_test.gd, seed=1337, T2 test 1)
1_release_no_repeat.evidence: committed JOIN to a host that wanders off + belief goes stale -> join.abort_ghost=1 fires, task releases to 建設 (not permanent latch), join_rejected memory written on leader (decision_context:530 cooldown), social_target cleared -> same host cannot be re-picked within cooldown window = churn cannot repeat costume by construction, not just observed-to-be-lower
1_release_no_repeat.caveat: organic-run same-pair-repeat counts for the 2mo branch/base runs were lost (wrapper stdout-corruption on timeout-kill, see tooling_finding below); this control-bed proof is considered stronger evidence per measurer protocol (control-scenario causal proof > organic aggregate noise) and stands in for the organic count

2_churn_resolved_ratio.note: base's ratio (300%) is NOT a meaningful 'better than branch' signal -- n=3 commits over 35 days on plain (non-agriculture-b) config is too small a sample (consistent with attribution finding: natural churn incidence on plain main is low-volume; original 1.4% figure came from agriculture-b's high-stress 698-commit sample, a different scenario). The TDD control-bed proof above is the reliable evidence for ratio-recovery; branch's 40% resolve rate against 15 commits in the same window is directionally consistent with recovery.

6_probe_true_fire.evidence: join.timeout and join.abort_ghost both independently fired with real state changes (task release, memory write, social_target clear) in the deterministic control bed; also join.timeout=1/abort_ghost=3 fired in the organic branch day35 run

8_fp_intended_change_churn_rich.note: not re-run byte-identical determinism myself (implementer's own claim: TDD 7/7 + determinism byte-identical x2); independently corroborated the 'intended change is live, not dead code' claim via control bed (item 6)

tooling_finding.summary: tools/godot.ps1 wrapper has a race: on GODOT_TIMEOUT-triggered Kill(), the immediately-following [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($tempOut) can throw 'file being used by another process' (killed process hasn't released its stdout redirect handle yet) -> ALL stdout for that run is lost, only the sidecar/side-channel (if the bed writes one) survives
tooling_finding.reproduced: twice, once under concurrent godot.ps1 invocation (could be dismissed as concurrency) and once solo (rules out concurrency as the sole cause -- this is a general timeout-kill race)
tooling_finding.impact: any long organic run that hits GODOT_TIMEOUT loses its full stdout; only sidecar-style incremental dumps survive
tooling_finding.recommendation: route to systems as a separate tooling defect; workaround used this round = read the bed's sidecar checkpoint file instead of relying on wrapper stdout when a run times out
